blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: The Lunchbox Carriers of Mumbai
blocks.body:
Every working day in Mumbai, India, around 5,000 delivery workers known as dabbawalas carry about 200,000 home-cooked lunches from people's homes to their offices, and then return the empty lunchboxes in the afternoon. The system has operated for more than 130 years, and remarkably, it ( 19 ). Most dabbawalas have little formal education, and the system relies on simple tools: bicycles, trains, and a code of colors and symbols painted on each box.
Business experts from around the world have studied the dabbawalas to understand ( 20 ). One key factor is teamwork. Each box passes through several hands during its journey, and each worker is responsible for only one small part of the route. If one worker is sick, others in the group cover for him. Moreover, the dabbawalas are partners in a shared organization rather than employees of a company, so ( 21 ). Many observers believe that this shared responsibility is the real secret of the system's reliability.

o: is run by a large company
qs.ex: remarkably(驚くべきことに)のあと、教育を受けていない人々が単純な道具で運営していると続くので、「めったにミスをしない」。

o: how to replace it with apps
qs.ex: このあとチームワークなど成功の要因を説明しているので、「どうしてこれほど効率よく機能するのか」。

o: each worker feels a strong sense of ownership
they can choose their own working hours
new workers are hired every year
qs.ex: 社員ではなく共同経営者なので「一人ひとりが当事者意識を持っている」。最後の文の shared responsibility にもつながります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: The Purpose of Stripes
blocks.body:
Why do zebras have stripes? Scientists have proposed many explanations over the years. Some suggested that the stripes help zebras hide from lions by confusing them, while others believed that the pattern ( 22 ). However, none of these ideas was supported by strong evidence.
In 2019, a team of researchers tested a different theory. They dressed horses in coats with black-and-white stripes and observed how flies behaved around them. Compared with horses wearing plain coats, the striped horses ( 23 ). The flies approached them in the same way but seemed unable to slow down and land properly, often flying past or bumping into them.
This finding is important because biting flies in Africa carry dangerous diseases. ( 24 ), the researchers believe that stripes may have evolved mainly as protection against insects rather than against large predators.

qs.ex: しま模様の役割の仮説として自然なのは「体温を下げる」。ライオンを引き寄せるのでは逆効果です。

o: had far fewer flies landing on them
qs.ex: 次の文で、ハエが減速できずにうまく止まれなかったとあるので「止まるハエがずっと少なかった」。
ハエが病気を運ぶ→「そのため」しま模様は虫よけとして進化したと考えられる、という因果関係。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: A Glue That Did Not Work
blocks.body:
In 1968, Spencer Silver, a chemist at the American company 3M, was trying to develop a very strong glue that could be used in building airplanes. Instead, he created the opposite: an adhesive that was weak enough to be removed easily and could be reused many times without leaving any marks. Silver believed his discovery must be useful for something, and for several years he presented it to colleagues within the company. However, nobody could think of a practical product that would use it.
The answer finally came from Art Fry, another 3M scientist who sang in a church choir. Fry used small pieces of paper to mark the pages of his songbook, but they kept falling out. In 1974, he remembered Silver's glue and realized that it would allow him to make bookmarks that stayed in place but could be removed without damaging the pages. Fry and Silver then developed the idea into small notes that could be stuck on almost any surface.
Even so, the product was not an immediate success. When it was first tested in a few cities in 1977, sales were disappointing, partly because customers did not understand what it was for until they tried it. The company therefore decided to give away large numbers of free samples, and once people began using the notes, they quickly became hooked. Launched across the United States in 1980, the notes went on to become one of the best-selling office products in the world.

qs.q: What was Spencer Silver originally trying to do?
o: Develop a new type of paper.
Make a glue that could be removed easily.
qs.ex: trying to develop a very strong glue とあります。はがせる接着剤は「逆」の結果でした。

qs.q: How did Art Fry come up with a use for Silver's glue?
o: He saw colleagues using it at a meeting.
He read about it in a science magazine.
He had trouble keeping bookmarks in his songbook.
He was asked by 3M to find a use for it.
qs.ex: 聖歌隊の歌集にはさんだしおりが落ちてしまうことから思いつきました。

qs.q: Why were early sales of the notes disappointing?
o: They were too expensive for most offices.
They did not stick to most surfaces.
3M did not advertise them at all.
People did not understand their purpose until they tried them.
qs.ex: customers did not understand what it was for until they tried it とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: When Volcanoes Ground Airplanes
blocks.body:
In April 2010, a volcano in Iceland called Eyjafjallajökull erupted, sending a huge cloud of ash high into the atmosphere. Winds carried the ash toward Europe, and within days, much of the continent's airspace had been closed. Over about a week, more than 100,000 flights were canceled and around 10 million passengers were unable to travel, making it the largest disruption to air travel in Europe since the Second World War.
To many travelers, the decision to stop flights seemed extreme. After all, the ash cloud was often invisible from the ground, and the sky looked clear. However, aviation experts knew that volcanic ash is extremely dangerous for jet engines. Unlike the ash produced by burning wood, volcanic ash consists of tiny pieces of rock and glass. When it enters a jet engine, which operates at temperatures of over 1,000°C, the ash melts and then sticks to parts inside the engine as it cools, which can cause the engine to stop.
This danger was first clearly demonstrated in 1982, when a British Airways Boeing 747 flew into an ash cloud from a volcano in Indonesia at night. One by one, all four of its engines stopped, and the plane began to glide toward the ground. As it descended into cleaner air, the crew managed to restart the engines, and the plane landed safely. The incident led to the creation of special centers around the world that track volcanic ash and warn pilots.
After the 2010 eruption, however, airlines complained that the rules were too strict. At the time, any amount of ash was considered unsafe. Following tests with engine manufacturers, authorities introduced a new system that allows planes to fly through areas with low concentrations of ash. Today, airlines can make decisions based on more detailed information, so a similar eruption would likely cause far less disruption.

qs.q: What happened as a result of the 2010 eruption?
o: Millions of air passengers were unable to travel.
Flights were moved to airports in Iceland.
Planes flew lower to avoid the ash.
qs.ex: around 10 million passengers were unable to travel とあります。

qs.q: Why is volcanic ash dangerous for jet engines?
o: It melts inside the engine and sticks to its parts.
It burns and creates too much heat.
It blocks the pilots' view of the sky.
It makes the engines use more fuel.
qs.ex: 岩やガラスの粒が高温のエンジン内で溶け、冷えて部品に付着するためです。

qs.q: What was one result of the 1982 incident?
o: Centers were set up to track ash and warn pilots.
Airlines began flying only during the day.
qs.ex: The incident led to the creation of special centers ... that track volcanic ash and warn pilots とあります。

o: Airlines were banned from flying near Iceland.
Engines were redesigned to burn ash.
Any amount of ash came to be considered unsafe.
Planes were allowed to fly through areas with low levels of ash.
qs.ex: 低濃度の火山灰の中なら飛行できる新しい仕組みが導入されました。「どんな量でも危険」は以前の規則です。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は60語〜70語です。
parts.body:
In many countries, including Germany and Norway, people pay a small extra charge, called a deposit, when they buy drinks in plastic bottles or cans. When they return the empty containers to a store or a special machine, they get the deposit back. Several other countries are now considering introducing similar systems.
Supporters point out that these systems are highly effective. In some countries with deposit systems, more than 90 percent of bottles are returned, far higher than in countries that rely only on ordinary recycling. Because the containers are collected separately, they are also cleaner, which makes it easier to turn them into new bottles.
However, critics argue that such systems have drawbacks. Stores must provide space and staff to collect containers, and installing return machines can be expensive. Moreover, some consumers find it inconvenient to store empty bottles at home and carry them back to shops.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Some countries, such as Germany and Norway, add a refundable deposit to drink containers, which customers get back when they return them, and other countries are considering similar systems. These schemes work well, with over 90 percent of containers returned, and the clean containers are easier to recycle. However, they require space, staff, and expensive machines in stores, and some consumers find returning bottles inconvenient.
checks: デポジット制度とは何か(返却するとお金が戻る・導入を検討する国がある)が入っている
利点(高い回収率・きれいで再利用しやすい)が入っている
問題点(店の負担・費用・消費者の手間)が入っている
本文をそのまま写さず、言いかえて短くまとめている
語数が60〜70語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Should all cyclists be required by law to wear helmets?

POINTS
・Safety
・Personal freedom
・Convenience
rules: 語数の目安は120語〜150語です。
構成は、序論・本論・結論が望ましい。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model:
I believe that all cyclists should be required by law to wear helmets, for two main reasons.
First, helmets greatly reduce the risk of serious injury. In bicycle accidents, head injuries are the most common cause of death, and studies show that wearing a helmet can significantly lower this risk. Since even careful riders can be hit by cars, everyone needs this protection.
Second, a legal requirement would change people's habits. At present, many cyclists, especially adults, do not wear helmets because they find them uncomfortable or think they look strange. If wearing one became a rule, it would quickly become normal, just as wearing seat belts in cars did.
In conclusion, because helmets save lives and a law would make wearing them a common habit, I support making helmets compulsory for all cyclists.
checks: 序論で自分の立場(賛成/反対)をはっきり述べている
POINTSなどを使った理由を2つ、具体例とともに書いている
本論の各段落が First / Second で始まり、構成がわかる
結論で立場と理由をまとめ直している
語数が120〜150語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Raj. Are you still planning to apply for the position in the London office?
I was, but I've been having second thoughts. My kids just started at a new school here, and moving them again so soon doesn't seem fair.
I understand. But opportunities like this don't come up very often.
I know. I'm going to ask whether I could start next year instead, once the school year ends.
That sounds like a sensible compromise.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Send his children to school in London.
Ask if he can delay his start date.
items.ex: 学年が終わる来年から始められないか聞くつもりです。

lines: Excuse me, I bought this coffee maker here last week, and it's already leaking.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have the receipt?
Thank you. We're out of this model at the moment, so I can either give you a full refund or order a replacement, which would take about ten days.
Ten days is too long. I'll take my money back and look for something else.
items.q: What does the man decide to do?
items.ex: I'll take my money back と言っています。

lines: Professor Davis, I wanted to ask about the research assistant position you mentioned in class.
Ah, yes. I'm looking for someone who can help analyze survey data. Have you taken the statistics course?
Not yet. I'm planning to take it next semester.
Well, the position starts in two weeks. I'd suggest taking the online statistics workshop the library offers this weekend. If you do that, I'd be happy to consider you.
items.q: What does the professor suggest the student do?
o: Wait until next semester to apply.
Attend a workshop offered by the library.
items.ex: 今週末の図書館のオンライン統計ワークショップを受けるよう勧めています。

lines: Honey, did you call the plumber about the kitchen sink?
I did, but he can't come until Thursday.
Thursday? We're having eight people over for dinner on Wednesday.
I know. My brother said he could take a look at it tomorrow evening. He fixed his own sink last year.
Well, if he can't fix it, we'll just have to order food in.
items.q: What will happen tomorrow evening?
o: The woman's brother will try to fix the sink.
They will have a dinner party.
They will order food for dinner.
items.ex: 女性の兄(弟)が明日の夜に見てくれることになっています。

lines: How's the new marketing campaign going?
Not as well as we'd hoped. The online ads are getting plenty of views, but very few people are actually buying the product.
Maybe the problem is the website. A lot of customers have complained that the checkout process is confusing.
That's a good point. I'll ask the web team to simplify it before we spend any more on ads.
items.q: What does the woman imply?
o: The website may be stopping customers from buying.
The ads should be shown on television.
items.ex: 購入手続きがわかりにくいという苦情から、サイトが購入のさまたげになっていると示しています。

lines: Jenny, are you coming to the team dinner on Friday?
I'd love to, but I'm flying to Seoul early Saturday morning for my cousin's wedding.
Oh, that's exciting. The dinner should end by nine, though.
True, but my flight leaves at six, so I need to leave home by three. I think I'd better get some sleep. Please say hi to everyone for me.
items.q: Why won't Jenny go to the dinner?
o: She has to attend a wedding on Friday.
She does not get along with her team.
She needs to rest before an early flight.
She has to work late on Friday.
items.ex: 土曜早朝の便に乗るため、睡眠をとりたいからです。結婚式は土曜日以降です。

lines: Hello, I'm calling about the Japanese language course at your school. I took a placement test online yesterday.
Let me check your results. You did very well on the reading section, but your listening score was lower.
Yes, I've mostly studied with textbooks.
In that case, I'd recommend our intermediate class, plus our weekly conversation sessions. They're free for students.
Great. I'll sign up for both.
items.q: What will the woman do?
o: Join a class and the conversation sessions.
items.ex: 中級クラスと週1回の会話セッションの両方に申し込みます。

lines: Lisa, the client wants the presentation moved up to Tuesday.
Tuesday? That only gives us two days. The design team hasn't finished the slides.
I know. I've already asked them to prioritize it.
OK. Then I'll cancel my meetings tomorrow and work on the sales figures.
items.q: What will the woman do tomorrow?
o: Ask the client for more time.
items.ex: 明日の会議を取り消して売上の数字に取り組みます。

lines: Have you decided whether to buy an electric car?
I'm still thinking about it. The government subsidy makes it cheaper, but there aren't many charging stations near my apartment.
Couldn't you charge it at work? Our company just installed chargers in the parking lot.
Really? I didn't know that. That would solve my problem.
items.q: What was the man's concern about buying an electric car?
o: He had few places to charge it.
His company did not allow parking.
items.ex: 家の近くに充電スタンドが少ないことを心配していました。

lines: Excuse me. My connecting flight to Chicago was canceled because of the storm.
I'm very sorry, sir. The next available flight is tomorrow at 7 a.m. I can book you on that and give you a hotel voucher for tonight.
Is there any way to get there today? I have an important meeting tomorrow morning.
There's a flight to Milwaukee in two hours. From there, it's about a 90-minute drive to Chicago.
I'll take that and rent a car.
items.q: How will the man get to Chicago?
o: By flying to another city and driving.
By staying at the airport hotel.
items.ex: ミルウォーキー行きの便に乗り、そこからレンタカーで向かいます。

lines: Dad, I'm thinking of taking a gap year before university.
A gap year? What would you do?
I'd like to work for a few months to save money and then volunteer abroad.
That could be valuable, but I'm worried you might lose the habit of studying.
I'll take an online course while I'm working.
Well, if you have a clear plan, I won't object.
items.q: What is the father's attitude?
o: He wants her to start university immediately.
He thinks she should work full-time.
He will accept her plan if it is well organized.
items.ex: if you have a clear plan, I won't object(しっかり計画があれば反対しない)と言っています。

lines: Have you seen the new schedule for the office renovation?
Yes. Our floor will be closed for two weeks starting Monday.
So where are we supposed to work?
Management says we can either work from home or use the meeting rooms on the third floor.
I'll work from home. The third floor is going to be really crowded.
items.q: What will the man do during the renovation?
items.ex: I'll work from home. と言っています。

lines: The Gimli Glider. In July 1983, an Air Canada Boeing 767 flying from Montreal to Edmonton ran out of fuel at an altitude of about 12,000 meters. The cause was a simple calculation error. Canada was switching to the metric system at the time, and the ground crew had calculated the fuel in pounds instead of kilograms, so the plane carried less than half the fuel it needed. With both engines stopped, the captain, who was an experienced glider pilot, managed to glide the plane to a former air force base at Gimli, Manitoba. All 69 people on board survived.

qs.q: What caused the plane to run out of fuel?
o: A leak in the fuel tank.
An error in calculating the amount of fuel.
A storm that made the flight longer.
qs.ex: キログラムではなくポンドで計算してしまった計算ミスが原因です。

qs.q: What helped the captain land the plane safely?
o: Advice from air traffic controllers in Edmonton.
A long runway at Edmonton Airport.
qs.ex: 機長は経験豊富なグライダーのパイロットでした。

items.title: The Gimli Glider

lines: How Dolphins Sleep. Dolphins must breathe air, but unlike humans, they have to decide consciously when to take each breath. This raises an interesting question: how can they sleep without drowning? Scientists have discovered that dolphins rest only one half of their brain at a time. While one half sleeps, the other half stays awake, controlling breathing and watching for danger. After a while, the two halves switch roles. This allows dolphins to keep swimming slowly and come to the surface to breathe even while they are resting.

qs.q: Why is sleeping a challenge for dolphins?
o: They live in very cold water.
They must choose consciously to breathe.
They are always hunted by sharks.
qs.ex: 人間とちがい、息をするたびに意識して決める必要があるからです。

qs.q: What do dolphins do while resting?
o: They sleep on the sea floor.
They keep both halves of the brain awake.
They rest one half of the brain at a time.
qs.ex: dolphins rest only one half of their brain at a time とあります。

items.title: How Dolphins Sleep

lines: Bathing Monkeys. In the mountains of Nagano Prefecture, Japanese macaques are famous for bathing in hot springs during the cold winter. This behavior was first observed in 1963, when a young female monkey entered a hot spring to collect soybeans that had fallen into the water. Other monkeys soon copied her. A study published in 2018 found that female monkeys who bathe in winter have lower levels of stress hormones, suggesting that the baths help them save energy and stay healthy in the cold.

qs.q: How did the monkeys' bathing behavior start?
o: A young monkey entered a hot spring to get food.
Park workers taught the monkeys to bathe.
The monkeys were trying to escape from danger.
An old monkey was injured and needed warmth.
qs.ex: 若いメスのサルが、お湯に落ちた大豆を拾うために温泉に入ったのが始まりです。

o: Male monkeys bathe more often than females.
Bathing may help reduce stress in winter.
Monkeys bathe only when there is food in the water.
qs.ex: 入浴するメスはストレスホルモンが低いことがわかりました。

items.title: Bathing Monkeys

lines: The Great Molasses Flood. On January 15, 1919, a huge storage tank in Boston, in the United States, suddenly burst. More than eight million liters of molasses, a thick, sticky syrup made from sugar, poured into the streets in a wave that was several meters high and moved at about 50 kilometers per hour. The disaster killed 21 people and injured around 150. A later investigation found that the tank had been poorly built and never properly tested, and the company that owned it was ordered to pay compensation. The case led to stricter rules for checking the safety of buildings.

o: A ship carrying sugar sank in the harbor.
A fire destroyed a sugar factory.
Heavy snow caused a building to collapse.
A tank burst and released a huge amount of syrup.
qs.ex: 巨大なタンクが破裂し、糖蜜(シロップ)が街に流れ出しました。

qs.q: What was one result of the disaster?
o: Molasses was banned in the city.
Stricter safety rules for buildings were introduced.
The company built a larger tank.
Boston became famous for its syrup.
qs.ex: The case led to stricter rules for checking the safety of buildings. とあります。

items.title: The Great Molasses Flood

lines: The Birth of the QR Code. The QR code was invented in 1994 by Masahiro Hara, an engineer at Denso Wave, a Japanese company that makes parts for cars. Factories at the time used barcodes to track car parts, but barcodes could hold only a small amount of information, and workers had to scan many of them. Hara's square code could store far more data and be read quickly from any angle. He reportedly got the idea from the black and white stones of the board game Go. Because the company chose not to use its patent to stop others from using the code, it spread freely around the world.

qs.q: Why was the QR code developed?
o: To help people pay for goods in stores.
To track car parts more efficiently.
To replace the board game Go.
qs.ex: 工場で自動車部品を管理するバーコードの不便さを解決するためでした。

qs.q: Why did the QR code spread so widely?
o: The company let others use it freely.
It was required by the Japanese government.
It was cheaper than printing barcodes.
Car companies paid to use it.
qs.ex: 特許を使ってほかの人の利用を止めなかったので、自由に広まりました。

items.title: The Birth of the QR Code

lines: Messages from the Past. Along the coast of northeastern Japan, there are hundreds of old stone markers known as tsunami stones. Some were placed hundreds of years ago, and many carry warnings such as "Do not build your homes below this point." In the village of Aneyoshi in Iwate Prefecture, residents followed the advice on such a stone and built their houses on higher ground. When the great tsunami struck in 2011, the water stopped below the stone, and the houses were not damaged. Experts say the stones show the importance of passing on lessons from past disasters.

qs.q: What is written on some tsunami stones?
o: The names of people who died.
Warnings about where not to build homes.
The dates when villages were founded.
qs.ex: 「ここより下に家を建てるな」のような警告が刻まれています。

o: People moved the stone to higher ground.
The houses were not damaged by the tsunami.
qs.ex: 津波は石より下で止まり、家は被害を受けませんでした。

items.title: Messages from the Past

lines: Attention, passengers. Due to a signal problem, the 8:50 express train to the airport has been canceled. The next express will depart at 9:50 and arrive at the airport at 10:25. Passengers who need to reach the airport earlier may take the 9:00 local train from Platform 4, which arrives at 9:55. Alternatively, a replacement bus will leave from the main entrance at 9:15, arriving at about 10:10.
items.q: What should you do?
o: Take the local train from Platform 4.
items.ex: 10時までに着けるのは 9:55 着の普通列車だけです。急行は10:25、バスは10:10着。
items.situ: You are at a train station. You need to get to the airport by 10 a.m. It is now 8:45. You hear the following announcement.

lines: Thank you for calling Pine Valley National Park. We offer several guided activities in August. The Sunrise Summit Hike is our most popular, but it's eight hours long and only for participants aged 12 and over. The River Kayak Tour is suitable for ages 8 and up. Our Wildlife Spotting Walk is a gentle two-hour walk for all ages, but it's fully booked in August. The Evening Star Program is held every night and is open to everyone, including small children.
items.q: Which activity should you choose?
items.ex: 7歳の子がいるのでカヤック(8歳以上)と登山(12歳以上)は不可。ウォークは満員なので、だれでも参加できる星空プログラム。
items.situ: You are planning a trip to a national park in August with your family, including two children aged 7 and 10. You want a guided activity that all of you can join. You call the visitor center.

lines: Hi, this is Dan from HR. Welcome to the company. About the parking permit: normally you apply online, but the online system is down until Friday. If you need a permit before then, please bring your driver's license and car registration to the security office on the first floor. The security office is open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., and temporary permits can be issued immediately.
items.q: What should you do?
o: Take your documents to the security office.
Call Dan in the HR department.
Park on the street until Friday.
items.ex: 明日までに必要なので、オンラインを待たずに書類を警備室へ持って行けばすぐ仮許可が出ます。
items.situ: You are a new employee. You need a parking permit for your car by tomorrow. You hear the following voice message from the HR department.

lines: The light show at the bay runs twice each evening, at 8 p.m. and 9 p.m., and each show lasts 15 minutes. From here, it takes about 30 minutes to get there by taxi, but at around 8 p.m. traffic is heavy, so it can take 50 minutes. The train is more reliable and takes about 25 minutes, including walking. You can also see the show from our rooftop bar, although the view is partly blocked by another building.
items.q: What should you do?
o: Take a taxi to the 8 p.m. show.
Take the train to the 9 p.m. show.
Take the train to the 8 p.m. show.
Watch the 9 p.m. show from the rooftop bar.
items.ex: 9時にはホテルにいる必要があるので9時の回は不可。8時の回に確実な電車で行けば、8:15に終わって8:40ごろ戻れます。
items.situ: You are staying at a hotel. You want to see the city's famous light show, but you have to be back at the hotel by 9 p.m. for a business call. The concierge tells you the following.

lines: Thank you for calling StyleHub customer service. Items can be returned within 30 days of purchase. If you have your receipt, you can return the item at any of our stores for a full refund. Without a receipt, you can exchange the item for store credit in our stores. You can also return items by mail using the prepaid label in your order email. Mail returns are free for members, but non-members pay a 500-yen fee. Membership is free and takes just a minute to set up on our website.
items.q: What should you do?
o: Return the jacket at a store for a refund.
Pay the 500-yen fee and return it by mail.
Exchange the jacket at a store.
Become a member and return it by mail.
items.ex: レシートがないので店での返金は不可、交換は返金ではない。無料で会員になれば郵送返品が無料です。
items.situ: You want to get your money back for a jacket you bought online 20 days ago. You have lost the receipt, and you do not want to pay any fees. You call customer service.
